# IdeaVim fixtures this host does not match yet.
#
# Generated by VimFixtureReplayTest, which writes the current list to
# build/fixture-failures.txt with the difference for each one, and a header saying how many were
# harvested and why the rest were not. To update this file, read that one and copy the names across
# - never edit a name by hand to make the build pass.
#
# 1940 of the 2081 harvested fixtures pass.
#
# The corpus has grown from 1,047 to 2,081 in four steps, and every one of them was the harness
# looking at less of `src/test` than it thought.
#
# It only found backtick-quoted test names, so IdeaVim's 578 plainly-named tests were *invisible*
# rather than refused. It only read a method whose body *started* with `doTest`, so a method that
# bound its text first, or called `doTest` more than once, gave up everything but the first call.
# It skipped the 1,039 `doTest` calls under `/extension/` wholesale, on a reason that stopped being
# true when twenty-two of the twenty-four extensions were ported. And it only read `doTest` at all,
# where 922 of IdeaVim's tests are written as `configureByText` / `typeText` / `assertState` - which
# is what `doTest` is a helper over. Each of those is a fixture per `assertState`, replayed from the
# top, so a method that checks, types `u`, and checks again is two.
#
# 141 of the 2,081 fail and 128 of them are one thing, which is the largest single finding this
# corpus has produced. See below.
#
# Two things the harness had to get right for these numbers to mean anything, both learnt from a
# fixture that was measuring the harness rather than the host:
#
# `u` is not the engine's here. This host asks VS Code to undo and holds the next keystroke until it
# lands - the right answer in a window, and no answer at all against a fake with no undo stack. The
# replay performs `undo` and `redo` on the fake now, out of the edit history it has kept all along.
#
# And an ex command is not the same as typing its keys. A mapping's body can contain `<Esc>`, and
# typing that at the command line presses Escape rather than writing five characters - which is why
# `doTest`'s setup commands are typed literally rather than parsed. Folding `enterCommand` into the
# key stream produced sixteen fixtures that measured the harness: `:nmap ,f iHello<Esc><CR>,fdh`
# left an empty buffer because the mapping was never defined.
#
# Before believing an entry in this file, check that the fixture passes in the plugin. Two of them
# did not - both were `@Disabled` over there, and the harness now skips those.

# --- `u` undoes a keystroke, where Vim undoes a command.
#
# 128 fixtures, one gap, and it is worth stating plainly because it is a bug a user meets in the
# first minute: `ciwfoo<Esc>u` puts back `fo`, not the word.
#
# This host's undo is VS Code's. A Vim command reaches the document as one `editor.edit` per
# *keystroke* - the flush is per keystroke - and VS Code's default is an undo stop before and after
# every edit an extension makes, so `u` walks back one keystroke at a time. IntelliJ is told where
# an undoable unit ends and this host is not: `VimKeyBasedUndoService.setMergeUndoKey`,
# `updateNonMergeUndoKey` and `setInsertNonMergeUndoKey` are all no-ops here, and the comment on
# them says the boundaries "are already where they belong" because the host "gives VS Code a whole
# command as a single edit". It does not; it gives it one edit per keystroke.
#
# `edit` takes `{ undoStopBefore, undoStopAfter }` and those three callbacks are the signal for it.
# That is the shape of the fix and it is not a small one, which is why these are recorded rather
# than papered over.
